2611.14681.image_caption: Figure 2 : TKCC ’s two-tiered measurement system outperforms a single slow tier, no measurement tiers, and Apple’s RSI inference bench harness on B200 GLM 5.3 optimization.

2611.17068.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of MAPE ’s program evolution framework. Candidate programs are proposed using archived designs and diagnostic feedback, checked for execution errors, and evaluated on the search set. Their implementations, results, and diagnoses are retained to guide subsequent proposals. Evolution follows either an accuracy-only objective ( MAPE-A ) or joint accuracy–cost objectives ( MAPE-P ). Shortlisted programs undergo held-out evaluation for final selection.

2611.17316.image_caption: Figure 2: What crosses coding-task boundaries and where memory is valued and optimized. Existing settings keep memory within one task, transfer general experience across independent tasks, or carry memory while resetting the repository. Our setting carries both repository state and memory to unseen future tasks. The ↺ \circlearrowleft and ↓ \downarrow symbols indicate whether memory is valued and optimized on its source task or on future tasks.

2611.14840.image_caption: Fig. 1: SPIRE learning architecture. From left to right: situation inference, primitive composition and recurrent-spiking action output. Colored dashed arrows indicate selection of source and residual actors, while the solid x t x_{t} arrow carries their current input. Paired event rows denote positive and negative population channels. Environment feedback supports context inference and local learning. The context-belief map and control environments are schematic.

2611.15178.image_caption: Figure 1: Parameter-space GRPO is costly, forgetful and opaque; HyperSkill instead keeps the backbone frozen and evolves a hypergraph-indexed skill library.

2611.15276.image_caption: Figure 1 : Active verification of a budget workbook. The task requires correct payer assignments, consistent expense totals, and after-tax revenue. Initial checks inspect labels and headers; an updated Evaluator skill retrieves expense and revenue cells while the workbook remains selected. Offline recomputation checks expense totals and after-tax revenue from the retrieved cells.

2611.15315.image_caption: Figure 12: Joint frontier on matched memory states after Qwen-to-Mistral handoff and continued writing. Higher answer quality and smaller private memory place a method farther toward the upper right. The ink stroke connects the two observed frontier points. Marker color shows quality retained relative to same-method rebuilding. Squares mark target-native references, shading follows QA/MB, and whiskers show 95% conversation-bootstrap quality intervals where available.

2611.15600.image_caption: Figure 1. Motivation of MemCredit. Semantic relevance does not necessarily imply decision utility. A memory that appears less related to the current observation may be critical for avoiding an incorrect action, whereas a highly relevant memory can be redundant.

2611.15700.image_caption: Fig. 2: The diagnostic workflow and its expert-review loop. Layers B and A produce retrieval and answer evidence, respectively. The ordered rule tree (3) assigns the initial route, and the agent judge (4) audits that decision. A human expert reviews the evidence and both rationales (5); those labels support harness changes to the rule tree and judge skills (6). The lower panels show the review interface for a turn on which the two routes disagree.

2611.17007.image_caption: Figure 1: The influence of user requirements on skill selection and composition. In contract translation, layout-preservation requirements affect document extraction and make layout reconstruction part of the subsequent workflow. Task descriptions and user feedback jointly inform skill adjustments and the selection of execution procedures.

2611.14949.image_caption: Figure 2: Examples of reference fields from public training cases. The benchmark includes diffusion and transport, fractional dynamics, wave propagation, fluid flow, phase-field systems and electromagnetics. The gallery is illustrative; Appendix B gives the complete 42-template catalog.

2611.15433.image_caption: Figure 1 : Verifier choice and verifier-use protocol change benchmark outcomes. Panel A shows a human-audited generated image. Panel B shows that the same image can receive different outputs under different verifiers and verifier-use protocols. Panel C reports aggregate metrics on the corresponding generator– object slices (Q4/Q27: Qwen3.5-4B/27B; G3n/G4: Gemma3n-E4B/Gemma4-E4B; FC/FR: few-shot count-only/reject-count), where the generated images and human labels are fixed but automatic scores and image-level agreement vary across verifier/protocol choices. This illustrates why a T2I benchmark score should be reported as a property of the generator, prompt distribution, verifier, verifier-use protocol, and scoring rule.

2611.15831.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of NIBench and the workflow evaluation tasks. a , The evaluation workflow. b , Distribution of the 56 workflow tasks by task tier, imaging modality and primary tool ecosystem. The inner and middle rings indicate task tier and imaging modality, respectively. Radial labels identify individual tasks, with text colors indicating the primary tool ecosystem. c , Example of a workflow task under protocol-guided and protocol-unspecified instructions. The protocol-unspecified condition removes the procedural instructions marked with a minus sign and adds the instruction marked with a plus sign. The task objective and output requirements remain unchanged.

2611.16064.image_caption: Figure 3: Large Thinking-OFF gains occur with both teacher inputs. A Thinking-ON teacher supervises Thinking-OFF rollouts. Columns vary teacher input. Rows vary evaluation mode and scale. U/F denote Unsolved/Frontier. Cells show three-seed Δ \Delta Avg@8 (pp) from Base.

2611.16591.image_caption: Figure 1: Singularity-Bench results across 11 frontier agents. The left panel shows the Singularity-Index versus agent API cost ( Section A.2 ). The Pareto frontier consists of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash + Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol + Codex, and Opus 5.5 + Claude Code (CC). The right panel shows each agent’s per-task scores, highlighting that Opus 5.5 + CC matches or beats the human solution on every task.
